questions.q: What is the Metasploit Framework, as described in this lesson?
options: A single proprietary 'hack button' with no modular structure
A tool that can only be used for passive reconnaissance, never exploitation
An open-source penetration testing platform, maintained by Rapid7, built around a structured library of versioned, community-vetted modules
A commercial vulnerability scanner with no connection to accredited certifications
questions.explain: Metasploit is an open-source platform maintained by Rapid7, built around a module library and a console, and it's the baseline framework referenced by PTES, OSCP, and CEH-style training.

questions.q: Why does Metasploit keep exploit modules and payloads as separate, independently selectable pieces?
options: Because payloads can only be used without any exploit module at all
Because exploit modules and payloads are actually the same thing with two different names
Because older versions of Metasploit did not support payloads
Because the same exploit module can be paired with many different payloads — 'how do I get in' and 'what do I run once I'm in' are treated as independent questions
questions.explain: The framework's architecture treats getting access and what to do with that access as separate concerns, so one exploit module can be combined with many different payloads.

questions.q: In a typical msfconsole workflow, what does the `check` command do, and when is it run?
options: It permanently deletes the selected module from the framework
It validates the vulnerability's presence non-destructively, and it's run before the `exploit` command
It is only available after `exploit` has already succeeded
It automatically generates a full written engagement report
questions.explain: check confirms the vulnerability is really present without running the full exploit, and it's a step a tester runs before committing to exploit.

options: An advanced, in-memory, scriptable payload that standardizes post-exploitation work like enumeration and pivoting across target operating systems
A standalone network scanner unrelated to Metasploit
A vulnerability database maintained by NVD
An encoder used only to obfuscate exploit module source code
questions.explain: Meterpreter is one of Metasploit's payload options — an in-memory, scriptable agent that gives a consistent post-exploitation interface across different targets.

questions.q: How does `db_import` connect Metasploit to earlier recon work from Chapter 3?
options: It has no connection to recon data and is used only for report formatting
It deletes any previously imported scan data automatically
It can pull an Nmap XML scan directly into a Metasploit workspace, making prior enumeration data searchable inside msfconsole
It is used exclusively to generate new payloads with msfvenom
questions.explain: db_import lets a tester bring an Nmap scan's XML output straight into a Metasploit workspace, turning earlier enumeration output into structured, searchable input for exploitation.
